quiz_item.scenario_prompt: When soldering electronic components onto a printed circuit board for Electronics Requirement 1, which safety practices protect your eyes, lungs, and static-sensitive integrated circuits?
quiz_item.question: When soldering electronic components onto a printed circuit board for Electronics Requirement 1, which safety practices protect your eyes, lungs, and static-sensitive integrated circuits?
options: A. Hold extra solder wire in your mouth while working, lean directly over the rising flux smoke, and rest the hot iron on the workbench mat.
B. Wear wool sweaters to build up static charge, flick excess molten solder off the tip with your wrist, and touch capacitor terminals immediately after unplugging a power supply.

C. Wear ANSI safety glasses to guard against solder splashes, use lead-free rosin-core solder in a well-ventilated area (avoiding flux fumes), return the iron to its heat-resistant stand, wear a grounded ESD wrist strap for static-sensitive chips, and wash hands after working.
D. Dip the hot soldering iron tip into a cup of cold water between joints and test whether the tip is hot by touching it with a fingertip.

patrol_quiz_bank.question: When soldering electronic components onto a printed circuit board for Electronics Requirement 1, which safety practices protect your eyes, lungs, and static-sensitive integrated circuits?

C. Wear ANSI safety glasses to guard against solder splashes, use lead-free rosin-core solder in a well-ventilated area (avoiding flux fumes), return the iron to its heat-resistant stand, wear a grounded ESD wrist strap for static-sensitive chips, and wash hands after working.
D. Dip the hot soldering iron tip into a cup of cold water between joints and test whether the tip is hot by touching it with a fingertip.

options: A. Permanently converting alternating current into mechanical motion
B. Storing electrical charge briefly and blocking direct current while passing alternating signals
C. Increasing the total voltage of a battery without an oscillator circuit
D. Acting as a sacrificial link that melts when current exceeds a safe limit
choices: A. Permanently converting alternating current into mechanical motion

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: B. Storing electrical charge briefly and blocking direct current while passing alternating signals
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (B): Capacitors consist of conductive plates separated by an insulator, allowing them to store electrical charge and block direct current (p. 38).
